chapter: Back in New York: Heard and Dizzy
title: Backing Etta Jones at Loew's State
summary: The band recorded behind Etta Jones and played the chilly Loew's State Theater, where she went over; he mentions her later work with Houston Person.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: and then after that the band broke up. But that was a great band. We did some recordings behind Etta Jones at the time. I'll never forget, we did Loew's State Theater, which was a big barn down here. And Etta Jones, may God bless her, they liked us all, but it was a very cold theater, but they loved her. And that impressed me. Etta Jones. I understand she's doing pretty well now.
Yeah. I saw her just recently, a few weeks ago, at the St. Charles Auditorium.
And she's got some fella that plays nice tenor, Pierson or something?
Yeah and they're together all the time. I heard a recording that they did. It sounded good. She's really singin' her heart out, yes she is.
So that was the first time that you had heard her and met her was at this time at the Cafe Society, must have been--what--'47, somethin'

Yeah, '46, umhum. I don't know what happened there. How she got with the band, I don't remember. But I know we did Loew's State together and she broke it up. That was a cold house. That's when I began to realize that Broadway can be a cold place, 'cause our applause was very chilly. Hahahaha.
